## The buyback wallet, reconciled (F2a, F2e, F2f)

That bought-back NEAR is held, not burned, is already public: SVRN's CEO said it is held in a "permanent capital vehicle", not destroyed ([Stocktwits, 2026-10-06](https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/cryptocurrency/near-treasury-firm-ceo-says-buybacks-are-still-real-but-issuance-runs-six-times-higher/cZDteDIRBl3)), and DefiLlama's methodology says "not burned". This repo adds a complete ledger for the wallet and explains the gap [Altcoin Buzz](https://altcoinbuzz.io/near-intents-has-bought-back-6-68m-of-near-using-fees) left open on 2026-10-19 between NearBlocks (2,015,496.446 NEAR in `buybacks.multisignature.near`) and revenue.near.org (1,510,410.8 NEAR).

- Ledger (F2a). In integer yoctoNEAR over all 2,732 rows, the RPC balance equals external revenue + 510,068 NEAR from `1csfundsadmin.sputnik-dao.near` (502,793 of it on 2026-09-09) - 12,025 NEAR out - 0.342 NEAR of fees for transactions the wallet signed, with 0 yoctoNEAR unexplained. The fees are 14 balance steps without a transfer row in FastNear's start/end-of-block balances.
- revenue.near.org is right about revenue (F2e). Its "Wallet Breakdown (All-time)" is each wallet's NEAR received from outside the three revenue wallets, not its balance. With the pre-2026 history of the two DAO wallets (in the M2 snapshot), all three rows match our inflow to the end of the previous UTC day within the page's 0.1 NEAR rounding. Refunded proposal bonds and transfers between the three wallets are excluded, which is right for revenue: the 510,068 NEAR forwarded by `1csfundsadmin` was already its revenue. DefiLlama also excludes them.
- The Altcoin Buzz gap (F2f). Both numbers are right. NearBlocks' is the balance at block 220,621,578; revenue.near.org's is external inflow to the end of 2026-10-17 (it lags about a day). The 505,085.6 NEAR gap = 510,068.0 internal - 12,025.0 out - 0.3 fees + 7,043.0 revenue after the cutoff, closing to 0.026 NEAR.
- Wording vs data. revenue.near.org says buybacks "permanently remove NEAR from circulation" (read 2026-10-20) and HSP-029 that they "stay removed". On chain the NEAR sits in an ordinary multisig whose signers have moved it three times (12,025 NEAR), and supply rose in every sampled interval (F2b). Both describe a policy, not an on-chain lock.

## Channel mix and meta-transactions (NEARData block sample, F5, F6)

Method. `pipeline/fetch_m2.py` draws 36 block heights per month of 2026, uniformly without replacement with `random.Random("20261020:<month>")`, between each month's first blocks after UTC midnight. A skipped height is replaced by the next block (1 of 360). NEARData (`https://mainnet.neardata.xyz/v0/block/<h>`) answers HTTP 429 beyond a burst of about 20 requests and about 0.23 blocks/s, so the fetcher spaces requests 3.8 s apart and backs off; the committed pull took 1,656 s. Per block it keeps a raw extract (`neardata_sample.jsonl`, 0.6 MB): every `EVENT_JSON` log from receipts on `intents.near`, verbatim, and each chunk transaction's receiver and action kinds. `compute.py` rebuilds the seeded plan and refuses a sample whose heights or order differ, so blocks cannot be added, dropped or swapped undetected.

Estimators. A *referred swap* is a dip4 `token_diff` entry with a `referral` tag (`1click-<channel>`, set by the 1Click API). A *meta-transaction* is a chunk transaction with a NEP-366 `Delegate` action. Blocks are clusters, so each share is a ratio estimate with variance from per-block residuals and a 95% Wilson interval at the effective sample size (units / design effect, at most the units). The 2026 row weights months by block count.

Results. 66 referred swaps in 360 blocks under 10 tags is too few for a monthly mix (3 to 13 a month), so the pooled row is the result: `1click-rango` (33% [21-47]) and `1click-swapkit` (27% [17-40]) lead, cannot be ranked, and neither has a majority (F5b). Noticed only after looking, so not asserted: Rango dominates January and February (11 of 14), SwapKit August to October (15 of 23).

Meta-transactions are far better measured: 79-87% of transactions in January to March, 45-65% in April to July, 30-36% in August to October (F6a: January and September intervals do not overlap). Transactions per sampled block fell from about 27 to about 6, consistent with one large relayed workload going away (January's design effect is 20). This replaces the prototype's 73-block pilot (78-88% in Q1, 22-30% in September and October): same Q1 range, somewhat higher September and October.

## Limits of the pipeline

- F1 is a consistency check, not independent proof. DefiLlama's revenue is "NEAR/wNEAR swept into its revenue wallets", the same data as ours, so F1 shows the public number reproduces from raw transfers with no timing shift, not that the wallets are the right ones.
- Only native NEAR counts. About $1.13M of USDC and other token inflows to the same wallets is excluded (`non_near_inflows_usd_excluded` in `metrics.json`), as in DefiLlama's NEAR/wNEAR definition.
- "Custody, not a burn" is about this wallet, not all possible burns: supply never fell between samples, and the wallet's only outflows are 3 transfers (two to `nf-payments.near`, one to an implicit account).
- The break-even figure assumes a burn that does not happen. The NEAR is held (F2), so supply grows at any volume; $795M/day is where buybacks would absorb new supply if burned (about 87,600 NEAR a day of purchases, independent of price).
- The break-even model is simple: fixed 30-day take rate and price, the whole net issuance (including the treasury's 10%) as the amount to offset, and fee burn estimated as "what a 2.5% cap would mint minus what supply actually grew". Volume is DefiLlama's; gross fees and full-year volume are not rebuilt from chain data.
- Data moves. A later `make data` changes the as-of date, price and volume; the assertions are statistical or structural, so a failure on fresh data is a real signal, not necessarily a bug.
- The block sample is small because NEARData is throttled. 360 blocks suffice for the meta-transaction share but are thin for channels (monthly intervals tens of points wide); `--per-stratum` scales it up. Channels cover only 1Click-tagged swaps: untagged intents (direct API users, solver legs) are outside, and `1click-unknown` is an integrator's tag, not a parsing gap.
- Published figures are pinned, not fetched. revenue.near.org renders client-side, so its values were read on 2026-10-20 and typed into `config.json` with the URL. F2e's previous-UTC-day cutoff is what the page matched on both readings (2026-10-17 for Altcoin Buzz, 2026-10-19 for ours).
- FastNear's transfers API returns HTTP 429 under bursts, so a fresh pull takes minutes.
